editorial:
Imagine living in a fancy London neighborhood with your best friends, just hanging out and not really worrying about the future. That is exactly where you find these four twenty-somethings. They have a great place and a laid-back lifestyle until a simple mistake changes everything. They let a total stranger into their home, thinking he is someone else or just a passing guest. At first, it seems harmless, but the vibe shifts quickly. You can feel the tension grow as this man slowly starts to run the house and manipulate the group, turning their safe space into a place of fear.

What really makes this work is how the acting makes the stranger feel genuinely creepy. The way he takes over is slow and steady, which keeps you on the edge of your seat. While some parts of the middle feel a bit slow, the payoff is worth it. If you love movies where a guest overstays their welcome in a scary way, you need to see this. You can rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night, or if you really love physical media, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your collection is the way to go for the best picture quality.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the stranger reveals he has been planning to steal the house and the friends' identities all along. After a tense fight, the group manages to trap him in the basement. Instead of calling the police right away, they realize they have become just as cold as he was. The movie ends with them deciding to keep him there, showing that the stranger actually changed them for the worse.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves psychological games and home invasion stories.
